header.running_head: The Enthusiasm of the Sahabah (RA) to Die and Give their Lives in the path of Allaah

blocks.text: Hadhrat Aasim (RA) also said the following:

I am Abu Sulaymaan with arrow made by (the expert arrow-maker) Muq'ad
And with a bow that is like a kindled fire
I feel no fear when a warrior comes storming on a speedy camel
And my shield is made from the hide of a bull with little hair
(To top it all) I am a firm believer in everything revealed to Muhammad ﷺ
He is also reported to have said:

I am Abu Sulaymaan and warriors like me are excellent archers
I am also from a tribe that is a most honourable one

Hadhrat Aasim (RA) then fought the Mushrikeen until he and his two companions were martyred. After killing Hadhrat Aasim (RA), the Hudhayl intended to severe his head to sell it to Sulaafa bint Sa'd bin Shuhayd. When her son was killed in the Battle of Uhud, she made a vow that if she ever got the head of Hadhrat Aasim (RA), she would drink wine from his skull. However, a swarm of wasps protected his body. When the Mushrikeen were prevented from getting to it, they said, "Leave him until the evening when the wasps would have left. We can then have him." Allaah then sent heavy rains flowing down the valley, which carried his body away.

Hadhrat Aasim (RA) had made a promise to Allaah that because the Mushrikeen were impure, none of them should ever touch him and he would not touch any of them either. When the news of the wasps protecting the body of Hadhrat Aasim (RA) reached Hadhrat Umar (RA), he said, "Allaah protects the Mu'min servant. Aasim (RA) vowed that no Mushrik should touch him and that he would not touch any Mushrik during his lifetime, so Allaah prevented it from happening after his death just as Allaah prevented it during his lifetime."
The Story of Hadhrat Zaid bin Dathana (RA) and his Statement About his Love for Rasulullaah ﷺ

(The other three Sahabah (RA) in the group) Hadhrat Khubayb (RA), Hadhrat Zaid bin Dathana (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Taariq (RA) chose the easier option and chose to remain alive. They therefore surrendered and were taken prisoner. The Mushrikeen took them to Makkah to sell them. When they reached a place called Zahraan, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Taariq (RA) slipped his hands from the bonds and grabbed a sword. The Mushrikeen stepped away from him started throwing rocks at him until they eventually martyred him. His grave is in Zahraan.

This left Hadhrat Khubayb (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Dathana (RA). they were taken to Makkah and exchanged for two prisoners from the Hudhayl who had been in Makkah. While Hujayr bin Abi Ihaab Tameemi bought Hadhrat Khubayb (RA), Safwaan bin Umayyah bought Hadhrat Zaid bin Dathana (RA) to execute him for the death of his father. Safwaan sent Hadhrat Zaid bin Dathana (RA) outside the Haram to Tan'eem with his slave Nistaas so that he could be executed there.
